title: Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocyte Networks on Multiwell Micro-electrode Arrays for Recurrent Action Potential Recordings
protocol: Thaw the coating substrate on ice or at 4 °C.
Dilute the coating substrate in cold DMEM/F12 medium by 1:100.
Mix the diluted coating substrate solution slowly.
Transfer 2 mL of the diluted coating substrate per well of a 6-well tissue culture plate.
Place the coated tissue culture plate in the cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for at least 7 h.
Add 10 mL of CM media supplement thawed at 4 °C to 500 mL of CM base medium.
Store the prepared hiPSC-CM culture medium at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Aliquot required amount of media and bring it to room temperature before use.
Mix fresh hiPSC-CM culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) to prepare thawing medium.
Bring the media to room temperature prior to thawing of CMs for suspension.
Aliquot 200 µL of fibronectin stock solution into 1.5 mL sterile microfuge tubes and store at 4 °C for later use.
Prepare a working solution of 50 µg/mL concentration of fibronectin freshly on ice.
Combine 0.5 g of enzymatic detergent with 50 mL of sterile double distilled water (ddH2O).
Vortex to mix the contents.
Filter and store the multiwell cleaning solution at 4 °C for up to a week.
Reconstitute cryopreserved hiPSC-CMs by placing vials in a 37°C water bath.
Swirl the vial gently for even thawing, not exceeding 3 minutes.
Transfer the contents of the vial to a tube containing FBS and mix by swirling.
Centrifuge the mixture at 200 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in hiPSC-CM thawing medium using gentle trituration.
Add additional thawing medium to further dissociate cell clumps.
Dispense 2 mL of cell suspension gently into each well of substrate-coated 6-well plates.
Place the plates in a cell culture incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Replace with fresh hiPSC-CM culturing medium after 24 h and 3 times weekly thereafter for 20 days.
Sterilize multiwell MEA plates under UV light inside a laminar flow hood overnight.
Add 0.5 mL of hiPSC-CM culture medium to each well two days prior to cell plating and perform a baseline recording.
Aspirate the media from the wells and rinse with sterile ddH2O.
Add 0.1 mL of FBS to each well for hydrophilic treatment of MEA surfaces.
Incubate the FBS in the wells for 30 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the FBS from the wells.
Rinse each well twice with 0.5 mL of sterile ddH2O.
Leave the plate to dry in the laminar flow hood overnight.
Prepare a working dilution of 50 µg/mL fibronectin in cold DMEM/F12 medium from the stock.
Keep the fibronectin solution on ice.
Pipette 5 µL of the working fibronectin dilution.
Carefully dispense the droplet to the center of each well to cover all 12 electrodes.
Place the fibronectin-coated multiwell MEA plate on a raised surface inside a humidifying chamber containing sterile ddH2O.
Cover the entire dish surface with water in the chamber.
Place the chamber with the multiwell MEA plate for 3 h in the cell culture incubator.
Aspirate the culture medium from each well of the 6-well tissue culture dish.
Wash each well with 2 mL of sterile D-PBS.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed cell dissociation solution per well and incubate for 4 min at 37°C.
Triturate cells gently with a transfer pipette to loosen them for dissociation.
If most of the cells are still adherent, incubate for another 3 min at 37°C and tritrate again.
Pool all the dissociated cells into a conical tube containing hiPSC-CM thawing medium.
Suspend cells in at least twice the volume of media (2 mL per well being harvested).
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend the pellet carefully by gentle trituration with a transfer pipette using 0.1 ml of hiPSC-CM thawing medium.
Aliquot 2 μL of dissociated cells and dilute with 18 μL of media in a microfuge tube.
Add 20 μL of Trypan Blue to the diluted sample for cell count and viability assessment.
Adjust the cell density to 6,000 cells/μL by adding appropriate volume of hiPSC-CM thawing medium.
Bring the multiwell MEA plate into the laminar flow hood for cell seeding.
Remove the fibronectin droplet using a P10 pipette without touching the electrodes.
Dispense a 5 μL cell droplet (30,000 cells) to the center of the well covering all 12 electrodes.
Repeat the step until all 24 wells are plated.
Intermittently mix the cell suspension by flicking during plating.
Place the multiwell MEA plate back in a loosely covered humidifying chamber.
Return the multiwell MEA plate to the cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 h.
Carefully add 200 μL of hiPSC-CM thawing medium to each well without disturbing the cells using a P200 pipette.
Add the media dropwise to the side of the well.
Replace with fresh hiPSC-CM culture medium at 24 h post plating.
Observe spontaneous beating of cardiomyocytes.
Change the media every 2 days until the end of experiments.
Turn on the interface board.
Initiate the acquisition software.
Allow time for the multiwell MEA headstage to reach 37 °C.
Insert the multiwell MEA plate into the multiwell MEA headstage.
Click the Insert button to confirm insertion.
Adjust temperature until stable before starting recordings.
Click on the Define Experimental Flow icon.
Set recording time to 2 min or as desired.
Click on the Data Acquisition Setup icon.
Set sampling rate to 20 kHz.
Set high-pass filter to 0.1 Hz.
Set low-pass filter to 3500 Hz.
Click on the Stimulator Settings icon.
Define stimulation as biphasic symmetric voltage pulses of 1 mV, 1 ms and 1 Hz under the Stimulus Definition tab.
Select electroporation sites by highlighting all relevant electrodes under the Stimulation Electrodes tab.
Click the Explore button to visualize signals in all wells.
Verify signal quality and steady state conditions.
Take notes on electrodes with FP signals in the mV range.
Click the same button to stop the exploration.
Start recording by clicking on the Go! button.
The electrodes in each well will show FP signals in the raw data window.
After 30 s of recording, click on the Stimulate button and allow electroporation to take place on the selected sites for 30 s.
Click on the same button to stop stimulation and continue recording for the remaining 60 s.
Aspirate all media contents from each well in the multiwell plate carefully avoiding touching the electrode surface.
Add 1 mL of sterile ddH2O per well.
Aspirate and repeat once with sterile ddH2O.
Add 0.3 mL of multiwell cleaning solution per well.
Incubate overnight at room temperature to dislodge cells and debris.
The following morning, aspirate the solution and rinse with 1 mL of sterile ddH2O.
Incubate for 5 - 7 min and aspirate.
Repeat 5 times with sterile ddH2O.
Add 0.5 mL of sterile ddH2O per well.
Record the baseline of the cleaned multiwell plate for quality check of the cleaned MEAs.
Store at 4 °C until ready to use.
Initiate the converter software.
Select Set Input Path from the File menu.
Select folder containing data files of interest.
Select Set Output Path from the File menu.
Select folder where converted files are to be saved.
Highlight MWD file of interest.
Click the EXPORT to HDF5 button.
Run the Waveform Analysis code using Matlab.
Click on File and select Process .h5.
Find and select the mwd.h5 file created according to step 7 above.
Click on the Save Directory button to change the storage location of the output files.
Create a signal processing queue by selecting electrode/well combinations of interest.
Click on the Queue button to process selected combinations.
Edit the queue by clicking directly on Med Name / Med Concentration if cells were treated with drugs.
Click the Initialize Waveforms button.
Click on the Zoom In button.
Select the action potential area of interest with the cursor.
Click the Keep button.
Review the panels.
Peaks (red ‘x’) and troughs (yellow circles) are detected for every waveform.
The normalized action potentials are superimposed.
Move on to the next trace in the queue.
Repeat steps 8.8-8.9 for the rest of the electrode/well combination signals in the queue.
